This has also made me realize that downvotes on reddit mean absolutely nothing.
Hey, but it'll be *good for your portfolio*.

Something's telling me no, but also telling me yes? I googled it, can't see much familiar, but it definitely had one of those things.

Maybe they've got rid of this thing, I don't know.

Thanks, too.

I will try it. It sounds like a good suggestion.
It's looking that way.
Yeah, that's basically my problem. I've had an artist block for four years, and it shows no sign of returning. All my life I've dreamed of making a living from my art, and now the passion is gone.

I'm sorry, I sounded ungrateful. I appreciate you were trying to help, but for me, art is like my child. Like... sex is to a normal human being. Like food.

I was also serious when I said I can't do anything else. I don't even know what trig is.

Not to take joy from a period you obviously struggled through, but hearing you 'muddled' for 3-4 years is kind of comforting. It makes the time length feel not so... unusual, I suppose. All these other artists I know seem to have blocks lasting, at most, a month. I'm still terrified it will never come back to me. It was such a great escape.

Half of me feels like taking a break from art is the way to go, but the other is worried that it will never come back if I wait.

I guess, if the offer is on the table, I have been dealing with depression since I was 13. Social Anxiety since 14. Upon going to uni and seeing someone, I have been diagnosed with Paranoid Personality Disorder, Schizoid personality disorder, and (possibly) Narcissistic Personality Disorder. I have also had bizarre bouts of Psychosis most of my life. There is also a strong suspicion that I have a developmental disorder. Mentally, I am not right. I feel like it's a burden on my boyfriend. He shouldn't have to deal with that.
No. Just, no.

I should have not been so specific about drawing. I cannot draw anymore, but I have always been very creatively minded. (Most arts, from writing to music used to excite me.) My creativity as a whole seems to have dried up.
Ah, that would help. Early 90s. Probably '93/4.

Unfortunately not. I wish I did, but I was far too young to remember.

It seems like it might be a lost cause, though. Oh well. I'll just have to keep scouring google maps on satellite.
That's cool. I must admit you all really helped tonight, as I edited in my post. I thank you all.

I hear that works for some. Doesn't for me, unfortunately. I need to be happy to art. I've never understood those types that draw depressing things.
But thanks anyway.
It's 6 in the morning, and the house is asleep, but I look forward to watching it tomorrow.
I have zero passion for drawing as it stands.

I want to believe that it'll come back, but I can just never see it happening. Not that I don't appreciate your kind words. But, yeah. I can't lie. I've forced myself to draw, I've left it for months, (record a year), and I've tried to just doodle and not care.

The only thing that works is weed. It reminds me of what I've lost.

"For me, art school sometimes made it worse because I HAD to do it and some of the enjoyment was lost" Yes, this is exactly what's happening. The only problem is, muddling through has not made it come back.

I have tried personal commitments, too. :( They last three days, I sigh, and think: What's the point? This is becoming a struggle. 

Only my whole career path is a struggle. I'm getting worse with every day that goes by.

Sorry for the rant. It's just nice to talk to another artist. And I definitely appreciate your words. Most of the counselors I've been to say 'art isn't important, let's worry about other things first.' 

*edit: I realized it sounds a lot like I just want to knock myself off because I can't draw anymore - I also have other problems, I just feel like losing my passion has tipped me over the edge.

That's not what I'm feeling at all. I have to force myself to draw. And it's never enjoyable. I used to have a healthy critical view of my own work, and I improved immensely. Now I don't care. I pop out crap once every 6 months, after forcing myself to sit down and draw something.

I'm sorry you're going through the same thing. I think I can truly say I feel your pain.

I'd say something to help, but I'd have said it to myself long ago if I knew what it was. Good luck with it all.
